exclusions: Do not select or implement one universal physical memory backend as Agent Memory doctrine.
Do not move Qortara Agent Governance, AgentTrust, QOR Agent, or provider-specific semantics into Agent Memory ownership merely for convenience.
Do not require Agent Memory to implement every cognitive algorithm internally when a qualified pluggable implementation preserves the contract.
Do not convert this roadmap into implementation-task nodes; implementation begins only after a legal /qor-plan handoff.
success_conditions: Canonical semantics for identity, evidence, lifecycle, PAMA, scope, recall, correction, deletion, inheritance, and cognitive composition are stable and internally coherent.
A supported runtime API executes those semantics without requiring consumers to depend on reference-package internals.
Canonical memory state and governance-critical state survive or reconstruct correctly across process restart.
At least one production-capable canonical persistence/deployment profile is qualified.
Additional memory capabilities can be deterministically discovered, qualified, composed, replaced, and removed without changing semantic authority.
Every mandatory runtime role for the 1.0 profile has at least one qualified implementation.
No provider, estimator, remembered procedure, confidence score, or retrieved state can manufacture mutation, recall, structural, or action authority.
Correction, supersession, dispute, rejection, readmission, and forgetting work end to end with reconstructable evidence.
Portable identity, trust, and execution-evidence integration exists without surrendering Agent Memory semantic ownership.
A real external agent runtime consumes Agent Memory successfully across multiple sessions and failure cases.
Operators can inspect health, currentness, residue, disputes, provider state, scope violations, decisions, and recovery.
The runtime has versioned releases, compatibility guarantees, migration procedures, security guidance, and production-readiness evidence.
objective.title: Bring Agent Memory from a governed reference architecture and evidence harness to a complete, independently deployable governed cognitive memory system suitable as a foundational Qortara OS primitive.

node.title: Reconcile current product truth: reference architecture/evidence maturity versus supported standalone runtime maturity.
Confirm the restart-safe governed runtime baseline already earned by completed issue #282.
Confirm ADR-035 three-plane governed cognitive framework is accepted canonical doctrine.
Confirm component/capability routing and qualification infrastructure already delivered versus still reference-only surfaces.
Set Agent Memory/PAMA as canonical owner of adaptive-state and memory-mutation semantics; Qortara consumes rather than redefines them.
Determine the smallest stable supported Agent Memory runtime API and package boundary beyond diagnostic/reference internals.
Compare historical Qortara evolution/adaptive-state implementation against current Agent Memory/PAMA and identify any unique behavior that must migrate or remain as an adapter.
Determine the production PAMA evaluator/enforcement profile, policy/version binding, approval verification, stale-decision protection, and receipt contract required for Agent Memory 1.0.
Determine the production canonical-state and governance-metadata persistence profile(s), including restart, idempotency, concurrency, migration, deletion, and recovery obligations.
Reassess EvolveAI, CodeGenome, COREFORGE Vault/Neurospace, and other first-party candidates against current capability qualification evidence and 1.0 needs.
Review remaining Proposed ADRs for evidence already earned versus genuinely missing acceptance work.
QOR Agent proving-ground integration #332 has completed with independently attributable multi-run Agent Memory evidence.
Determine the 1.0 portable trust/evidence profile across Agent Manifest, TRACE, cMCP, and governance peers without authority inversion.
Define the production operations, observability, security, compatibility, migration, release, and support obligations for Agent Memory 1.0.
Determine which Cognitive, Reality, and Authority plane roles are mandatory for 1.0 and which may remain optional/qualified-provider surfaces.

payload.rationale: The repository explicitly presents Agent Memory as a reference architecture with repository-validated doctrine/evidence, while the installable package remains agent-memory-reference and the public CLI is primarily validation/discovery/diagnostics rather than the complete consumer memory API.
Issue #282 is closed completed and records the earned restart-safe governed runtime baseline; 1.0 planning should build from this evidence rather than reopen restart durability as if nothing exists.
ADR-035 is Accepted and establishes Agent Memory as a governed cognitive framework with Cognitive, Reality, and Authority planes, shared Cognitive Mesh semantics, and PAMA-governed consequence.

The component/capability registry, deterministic routing, adapter/qualification contract, Capability Contract v3, and v3-bound qualification machinery are established foundations. Remaining work is qualification/composition/productization, not inventing another provider abstraction.

Repository owner explicitly directed that Agent Memory/PAMA own adaptive-state and memory-mutation semantics. Historical Qortara evolution behavior is implementation lineage to reconcile, not a competing semantic authority.

scope.title: Agent Memory 1.0 interoperability and production readiness
